product: KeyLoad development preview. Not production ready.
concept: Orleans owns all clustering and activation scaling. The API reaches one grain per connected client, logical database/partition grains, storage owners and bounded result aggregation. Shared volumes require one open owner per physical partition without copies; isolated volumes use typed Orleans calls between owners. Shared-volume ownership and distributed partition-query execution are not yet qualified.

evidence: Qualification evidence lives only in GitHub Actions runs and their original artifacts for the exact delivered source.
implementation: Orleans-execution runtime integration is in progress. The commit grain caches copy owners per membership version instead of reading every silo per write; KeyLoad owns no write-ahead log, backup, snapshot or archive format (ADR-011): ZoneTree 2.1.2 owns Shared WAL for MVCC and SyncCompressed WAL for direct resource data, a commit is one ZoneTree transaction that also holds the store position, acknowledgements require synchronous process-persistent WAL publication, opened native writers are checked before admission, and ZoneTree owns periodic disk sync, and a backup is the store identity plus one native LiveBackup snapshot generation per tree, with independent cuts, restored under a new identity with dispatch paused; the SQL gateway lowers SELECT once to the typed plan and the SDK carries no parser; stateless background workers sweep persisted work with one polling activation per silo and no in-memory buffer; internal grain requests are typed Orleans envelopes validated by scope on every receiving grain, with no per-hop string token or HMAC (ADR-144); native snapshots and serializable conflict retries replace application read/write gates; native maintainers replace the custom cache and cleanup timer; non-transactional tables use a separate native plain tree whose process-persistent WAL publication precedes transactional outcomes; key encoding takes typed components without boxing; the comparison harness has no warm-up phase anywhere. Request handling imposes no concurrency, request-count or reserved-byte admission on callers (ADR-145): the HTTP, command and MCP memory admission pools, the per-connection, per-silo producer and connection caps, the ANN reader caps, the per-engine analytical-read cap, the change-outbox producer quota and progress reserve, and the full-text reader and maintenance-session count caps are gone; only the server-wide request-body limit and the physical reply and protocol bounds remain, and the KeyLoad benchmark cells no longer carry an admission profile. Operations have no configured size or work limits (ADR-149): KeyLoad:DatabaseLimits keeps only the optional queue transfer attempt policies; document size, JSON depth, batch, scan, result, SQL text/depth/token, read-byte, search-token, projection and fixed-deadline refusals are gone; reads count no bytes or records and stop only on caller cancellation, internal request envelopes carry no expiry, complete ranges page through the storage range page, recursive SQL, AST and JSON walkers fail with Validation only when the execution stack runs short, and results, pages and grain request streams have no byte or frame cap (pages are bounded by their record limits). Concurrent canonical commands commit in batches (ADR-146): the reentrant commit grain queues them, every copy applies a batch as one process-persistent ZoneTree commit with parallel copy calls, each command keeps its own canonical sequence and outcome, and a copy that missed the last batch is completed from its retained commands; the engine and store contracts have unit tests, while cluster throughput and fault qualification of the batch path remain open. Queries ordered by ascending document id continue after the last emitted id instead of an offset (ADR-147): a full scan seeks past that id and stops one row past the page, so reading a collection page by page reads each document once, and no query range read asks storage for more than its per-range maximum. Build and Tests first completes one strict solution build (ADR-148), then test jobs consume its compiled artifact without rebuilding. Each Aspire lane runs on its own runner with native discovered ports. The final job requires exact compiled test coverage without duplicate execution, and Release publishes a push to main only after this workflow succeeds for that commit. Each source revision retains its own qualification boundary. IsolatedVolumes uses silo-local full copies; SharedVolume acquires one physical session through an ordinary database activation and joins its borrowers before close. PartitionQuery and DistributedSearch dispatch bounded leaves through ordinary Orleans partition grains and pin one actual owner per logical partition. Workers and durable coordinators use typed owner reads. Complete runtime and delivered-source qualification is open. Ordinary operations without progress consumers now drain the shared Communication CQRS producer on each independent ordinary request grain and return a settled Orleans Task reply; progress consumers and composed operations retain native response enumeration. Independent requests still use separate execution grains, fresh persisted authority and joined cleanup. Focused local connection checks and small real SDK diagnostics pass; exact-source Linux runtime and benchmark qualification of this transport change remain open. Published bootstrap text generations now share one native read-only index among independent readers, check only the owned file set at publication, settlement and cleanup, and join retained readers before invalidation, retirement or shutdown. A focused local batch passed 39 functional-assembly executions, 10 process-assembly recovery cases and four real Aspire SDK/MCP authorization/readiness cases, with no unobserved notices in that batch. The single staged bootstrap build and three-generation physical ceiling remain; parallel cold scopes, complete catch-up, endurance and exact-source Linux qualification remain open. Native typed command inputs, request envelopes and replies now replace private nested encoded operation/result buffers. Five auxiliary MemoryStream paths use standard .NET buffer/hash APIs; real key-format controls passed 22 cases. Selected full-text generation qualification remains open; ZoneTree rewrites its own metadata on a clean reopen (ZoneTree issue 209), so KeyLoad no longer hashes engine-owned files (docs/Features/Search/FullTextProjection.md). Commands carry no fingerprint: a retry compares the public input shape of the retained command only when a stored outcome exists (ADR-140), and a resource incarnation is the creating command GUID. A selected full-text search checks the generation's manifest sequence instead of re-reading and hashing the source corpus, reuses the validated manifest and its record maps until the manifest file changes, and keeps the native index open between searches. No competitive performance claim follows from these local changes. Scalar EXPLAIN now describes the access path selected by the same planner used for execution, with seek fields, bound presence, residual fields, read cut, ordering, retained rows and projection; it neither scans candidates nor reports invented costs. Local profiling identified repeated resource-catalog decoding in the KeyLoad storage adapter. A read operation reuses one routing decision only within its immutable native snapshot, with complete key validation. Terminal vector-only searches retain exact top-K when fusion ordering permits it; hybrid and distributed branches retain complete rankings. Graph traversal supports full, vertex-only and count output with the same visibility and traversal semantics. Ordinary HTTP/SQL operations authenticate the credential subject and authorize at their database operation owner; metadata-consuming adapters retain current authority reads. Independent request execution grains remain. These changes carry no competitive or power-loss claim; see docs/implementation/jepsen-particledb-review.md. Partition keys write typed scopes and dynamic suffixes directly into the existing key buffer, without intermediate component lists. Internal decoding reuses Orleans' registered singleton typed serializer with independently pooled sessions. Key bytes, application envelopes, aliases and versions remain unchanged; literal-byte, component-boundary and complete serialization controls retain their qualification gates. Adjacent document mutations now reuse validated collection metadata and lifetime within their current transaction, and outbox appends retain the validated head while staging it after each entry. Fresh permissions, per-document revisions, indexes and persisted command outcomes remain in the same path. Complete-operation tests bound additional new-document point reads to one per added document. Longer local SDK diagnostics retain full body/revision verification for batches of 256 and 1,024; they do not establish sustained throughput or the requested 30,000 documents per second. Exact-source Linux qualification remains open; see docs/Features/DocumentStorage.md. Isolated-copy batch preparation now prefers the commit coordinator's selected local copy after retained gaps reach a shared canonical cut, preserving the required copy set and every persisted outcome. Real two-host preparation, replay and healthy continuation tests pass locally; exact-source Linux qualification and the unchanged indexed documents benchmark for this change remain open.
